name: Gerard Wertheimer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Gerard Wertheimer and his brother Alain own French luxury brand Chanel.
Gerard heads the company's watch division and lives in Switzerland.
His grandfather, Pierre, partnered with Gabrielle (Coco) Chanel, the company's namesake, in the 1920s.
Karl Lagerfeld, the public face of Chanel, died in 2019 at the age of 85. He had been the company's creative director for over 35 years.
forbes_facts: Alain and Gerard breed and race thoroughbreds. Their horses have won races at the French Derby and the Breeders' Cup Turf in the U.S.
Gerard and his brother own vineyards in the Bordeaux region in France and Napa Valley, California.

name: Nancy Walton Laurie
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Nancy Walton Laurie inherited a stake in Walmart from her father, Bud Walton, who helped his brother, Sam, build the retail giant.
When Bud died in 1995, Walton Laurie and her sister, Ann Walton Kroenke, received enough Walmart stock to make them both billionaires.
Walton Laurie and her husband, Bill, also own a portfolio of commercial real estate, several homes and a yacht.
They gave $10 million in 2013 to the University of Memphis, their alma mater.
Walton Laurie became interested in dance when her daughter was a teenager and sat on the board of trustees at Julliard.
forbes_facts: In 1998, Walton Laurie founded the Columbia Performing Arts Centre, a performing arts school for children through high school in Columbia, Missouri.
Walton Laurie and her husband purchased the NHL's St. Louis Blues in 1999. They sold the team six years later.

name: Matthew Prince
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Wikidata (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019)
forbes_bio: Matthew Prince cofounded the web infrastructure and security company Cloudflare in 2009.
Prince owns about 8% of the company, which he took public in 2019, and serves as CEO.
Pre-IPO, its investors included Google's venture firm CapitalG, Microsoft, Baidu and Qualcomm Ventures.
Before Cloudflare, Prince was a law professor and cofounded Unspam Technologies, which helped block spam content for clients.
forbes_facts: Prince worked as a ski instructor for six months in Park City, Utah when he was in his early twenties.

name: Zhang Congyuan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhang Congyuan is the chairman of Huali Industrial Group, a shoe manufacturer he founded in 2004. The company now has factories in China, Indonesia, Vietnam, Dominica and Myanmar.
Huali supplies to dozens of brands including Nike, Puma, UGG and Vans.
Zhang also cofounded Hong Kong-listed shoemaker Symphony Holdings, but sold his stake and is no longer with the company.
He shares the fortune with his wife and children.

name: Giuseppe De'Longhi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Giuseppe De'Longhi is chairman of De'Longhi SpA, which produces high-end coffee makers and espresso machines.
De'Longhi's son, Fabio, is the CEO of the company, which pulls in over $2 billion in annual revenue and sells products in more than 100 countries.
The company was founded in 1902 in Treviso, Italy as a small industrial manufacturing workshop. A century later, its headquarters remain in Treviso.
The company makes portable heaters, air conditioners, appliances for food preparation, cleaning tools and coffee machines.
In 2015, De'Longhi sold his majority stake in Italian industrial heating company DelClima to Mitsubishi Electric for $551 million.
forbes_facts: In the late 2000s after portions of The Plaza Hotel in Manhattan were redesigned as luxury condominiums, De'Longhi was reportedly one of the first to buy a condo.

name: Tom Morris
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Tom Morris founded TJ Morris, which owns discount retailer Home Bargains, in 1976.
One of seven children of a Liverpool shopkeeper, he is the third generation of his family to run a retailer.
Morris, who closely guards his privacy, reportedly used a bank overdraft to start his business at the age of 21.
Home Bargains stocks everything from health and beauty products to candy and toys, often bought at a discount from brands trying to offload product.
There are more than 550 Home Bargains stores throughout the United Kingdom, with plans to expand to as many as 1,000.
forbes_facts: Morris is a member of the 20 Miles More campaign, which wants the UK Government to extend the proposed HS2 high-speed railway to Liverpool.

name: Andrei Kozitsyn
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Until 2022 Andrei Kozitsyn was CEO of Ural Mining Metallurgical Company (UMMC), one of the top Russian producers of such commodities as copper, zinc, coal and gold.
Kozitsyn grew up in the Urals, where he studied metallurgy and later went to work as a mechanic at Uralelectromed, now UMMC's main factory.
Kozitsyn cofounded UMMC with Iskander Makhmudov, who was the group's president and his longtime partner.
In January 2019, UMMC opened the Korova (Cow) restaurant in the elite district of Yekaterinburg.
forbes_facts: President and sponsor of KHL hockey club named Avtomobilist, Kozitsyn plans to build an ice arena with 15,000 seats in Ekaterinburg in 2024.
Kozitsyn founded Military Equipment Museum, which has tanks and armored vehicles and planes.

name: Edward DeBartolo Jr
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Real estate magnate Edward Debartolo Jr. heads DeBartolo Holdings.
The Florida-based property development and investment firm owns a diverse real estate portfolio, including apartments, development sites and hotels in several states.
An NFL Hall of Fame executive, DeBartolo Jr. owned the San Francisco 49ers during the 80's and 90's when the team won five Super Bowls.
In 1998, he pleaded guilty to not reporting a bribe from a Louisiana government official. President Trump pardoned him in 2020.
His sister, Denise DeBartolo York, took controlling ownership of the 49ers in 2001; her family runs the team today.
DeBartolo joined his dad's real estate company in his 20s. A quarter of a century later he directed its merger with Simon Property Group.
forbes_facts: DeBartolo joined his dad's real estate company in his 20's. A quarter of a century later he directed its merger with Simon Property Group.

name: Takahisa Takahara
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Takahisa Takahara is president and CEO of Tokyo-listed Unicharm, a maker of personal care products, which his late father Keiichiro founded in 1961.
Unicharm makes MamyPoko brand diapers, sanitary napkins, face masks, alcohol-based wipes and other personal care goods.
Two-thirds of Unicharm's nearly $7 billion annual revenue comes from outside of Japan, mainly from other Asian countries.
Takahara's father Keiichiro died in October 2018.
